teaser: The Welsh pop-punk heirs: 'In Bloom', 'December', 'She's a God' — Neck Deep's 'Life's Not Out to Get You' became the defining pop-punk album of the 2010s revival. Their blend of skate-punk energy and emo confessionals made them the scene's biggest new band.

exploreAction.targetName: Neck Deep — Life's Not Out to Get You (2015) end-to-end
exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'December' — the acoustic-into-electric heartbreak anthem. Notice how the band's UK punk DNA shows in the double-time sections.

name: Turnover
teaser: The Virginia band who outgrew pop-punk: 'Humblest Pleasures', 'Cutting My Fingers Off', 'Dizzy on the Comedown' — Turnover's 'Peripheral Vision' swapped guitars for dreamy reverb and became one of the most beloved alternative albums of 2015. Their sound defined the 'dreamo' subgenre.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Dizzy on the Comedown' — the album's shimmering centerpiece. Notice how the bass and the layered vocals create the dreamlike haze.

name: Movements
teaser: The post-hardcore confessionals: 'Deadly Dull', 'Daylily', 'Skin to Skin' — Patrick Miranda's raw vocals and the band's emo-metal blend made 'Feel Something' one of the most acclaimed rock debuts of 2017. Their live show is catharsis on stage.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Daylily' — the song about supporting someone through mental illness. Notice how the quiet verses and the huge chorus carry the hope.

name: Don Omar
teaser: The king of the perreo: 'Danza Kuduro', 'Dile', 'Pobre Diabla' — Don Omar was the most dominant reggaeton artist of the mid-2000s, his album 'The Last Don' defining the genre's cinematic turn. His reggaeton-opera 'King of Kings' pushed the sound into stadiums.

exploreAction.targetName: Don Omar — The Last Don (2003) end-to-end
exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Dile' — the song that made him a star. Notice how the reggaeton beat and the romantic melody set the template for the genre.

name: Nicky Jam
teaser: The reggaeton comeback king: 'Travesuras', 'El Perdón', 'X' — Nicky Jam's career collapsed in the 2000s and resurrected a decade later with 'El Perdón' (with Enrique Iglesias), one of the most streamed Latin songs ever. His 'Fénix' era made him the genre's redemption story.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'El Perdón' — the global smash that revived him. Notice how the song's emotional verses made it a crossover phenomenon.

name: Wisin & Yandel
teaser: The reggaeton duo who conquered the world: 'Rakata', 'Sexy Movimiento', 'Algo Me Gusta de Ti' — the 'Dúo de la Historia' made reggaeton a global sound with their airtight chemistry. Their album 'Los Vaqueros' and their Olympic-opening ceremony performance cemented the legacy.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Rakata' — the duo's breakthrough hit. Notice how the two voices trade the hook, the yin-yang that made them the genre's top duo.

name: Anuel AA
teaser: The trap god of Puerto Rico: 'China', 'Secreto', 'Culpables' — Anuel's raw, drill-tinged trap and his prison-recorded rise made him the most controversial star of Latin trap. His marriage to Karol G and their public split became the genre's biggest soap opera.

exploreAction.targetName: Anuel AA — Real Hasta la Muerte (2018) end-to-end
exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Secreto' — the duet with Karol G recorded during their relationship. Notice how the trap beat frames the most personal lyrics of his catalog.

name: Natanael Cano
teaser: The corridos tumbados pioneer: 'Diamantes', 'Amor Tumbado', 'O Me Voy o Te Vas' — Cano fused traditional Mexican corridos with trap and R&B, inventing the genre that took over Latin streaming. At twenty, he made the accordion and the 808 coexist.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Amor Tumbado' — the corrido-trap hybrid that defined the sound. Notice how the accordion plays the melody while the trap drums carry the rhythm.

name: Fuerza Regida
teaser: The corridos tumbados superstars: 'JGL', 'Bebe Dame', 'Sabor Fresa' — Fuerza Regida's narcocorridos and their trap-tinged production made them the biggest band in regional Mexican music. Their 'Pa las Baby's' era with Grupo Frontera brought the sound to the mainstream.

exploreAction.targetName: Fuerza Regida — Pa Que Hablen (2022) end-to-end
exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Sabor Fresa' — the viral hit with the reggaeton-cumbia blend. Notice how the tuba and the accordion keep the banda roots under the modern production.

name: Eslabon Armado
teaser: The sierreño romantics: 'Ella Baila Sola', 'Jugaste y Sufrí', 'La Octava Maravilla' — Pedro Tovar's teenage ballads made Eslabon Armado the most streamed group in regional Mexican music. 'Ella Baila Sola' (with Peso Pluma) became the first regional Mexican song to top the Billboard Global 200.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Ella Baila Sola' — the song that made the genre global. Notice how the requinto guitar and the romantic vocals carry the whole arrangement.

name: Grupo Frontera
teaser: The norteño-cumbia revivalists: 'No Se Va', 'Un x100to', 'Bebe Dame' — Grupo Frontera's crossover with Bad Bunny and Peso Pluma took their accordion-driven cumbia to the top of the charts. Their 'El Comienzo' album is the sound of regional Mexican pop's new era.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Un x100to' — the Bad Bunny collaboration about heartbreak. Notice how the cumbia rhythm and the accordion make grief danceable.

name: Calibre 50
teaser: The banda kings of the 2010s: 'Cabo San Lucas', 'Aqui a la Distancia', 'Chao Chao' — Calibre 50 modernized banda with romantic, streetwise songwriting and became the most listened banda act of the decade. Their catalog runs from narcocorridos to tender ballads.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Aqui a la Distancia' — the song that broke them. Notice how the banda brass carries the melody like a full orchestra.

name: Los Dos Carnales
teaser: The sibling corrido duo: 'El Envidioso', 'Al Estilo Rana', 'Cabrón y Vago' — Poncho and El Tigre's old-school, ranchera-flavored corridos made them the traditionalists of the corridos tumbados wave. Their 2020 breakout showed that classic Mexican music could still rule streaming.

exploreAction.targetName: Los Dos Carnales — Los Dos Carnales (2020) end-to-end
exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'El Envidioso' — the corrido with the driving tuba. Notice how the duo's harmony vocals root the song in ranchera tradition.

name: Pepe Aguilar
teaser: The hereditary mariachi star: son of Antonio Aguilar, 'Por Mujeres Como Tú', 'Prometiste', 'Directo al Corazón' — Pepe has carried the Aguilar dynasty into the modern era with Grammy-winning mariachi and ranchera. His 'MTV Unplugged' is the genre's finest modern document.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Prometiste' — the ranchera ballad with the full mariachi. Notice how the three generations of Aguilar voices appear in the finale.

name: Alejandro Fernández
teaser: El Potrillo: the son of Vicente Fernández, whose 'Me Dediqué a Perderte', 'Se Me Va la Voz' and 'Hoy Tengo Ganas de Ti' made him the most successful ranchera-pop crossover of his generation. His voice, a lighter echo of his father's, carries the mariachi tradition forward.

exploreAction.targetName: Alejandro Fernández — Me Estoy Enamorando (1997) end-to-end
exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Me Dediqué a Perderte' — the ranchera ballad that defined his pop era. Notice how the mariachi strings swell under his voice.

name: Luis Fonsi
teaser: The ballad king who made 'Despacito': 'Despacito', 'Échame la Culpa', 'Date la Vuelta' — Fonsi's reggaeton-pop smash with Daddy Yankee became the most-streamed song in history, and his ballad catalog ('No Me Doy por Vencido') had already made him a Latin star. 'Despacito' changed what a Latin pop song could be.

exploreAction.targetName: Luis Fonsi — Despacito (2017) — the album Vida (2019) highlights
exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Despacito' — the song that broke the internet. Notice how the original's bilingual verses and the reggaeton beat made it a global anthem.

name: Enrique Iglesias
teaser: The most successful Latin crossover artist in history: 'Bailando', 'Hero', 'Escape', 'Duele el Corazón' — Enrique's bilingual pop made him the top-selling Latin artist ever with over 180 million records. His catalog spans romantic ballads and reggaeton-pop anthems.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Bailando' — the Spanish-language smash that topped 35 countries. Notice how the flamenco intro and the dance beat blend seamlessly.

name: Danna Paola
teaser: The Mexican triple threat: from telenovela child star to 'Élite' fame to the pop-R&B of 'SIE7E +' and 'K.O.' — Danna's 'Oye Pablo' and 'Mala Fama' made her one of Latin pop's most exciting young voices. Her live vocals are the genre's best-kept secret.

exploreAction.instruction: Listen to 'Mala Fama' — the alt-pop hit about embracing the reputation. Notice how her voice, schooled in musicals, powers the chorus.
